extracted.intended_audience: Navy/DoD program managers, contract administrators, and researchers implementing or evaluating OMB Circular A-76 cost-comparison studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for carrying out OMB Circular A-76 Commercial Activities (CA) cost-comparison studies in the Navy: selecting activities, preparing Performance Work Statements, creating a Most Efficient Organization (MEO), developing in-house cost estimates, comparing to contractor bids, and handling post-award quality/transition issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-phase CA process
rubrics_metrics.description: The process involved in implementing the policy outlined in OMB Circular A-76 consists of basically four phases: inventory, management review, cost comparison, and implementation of the results of the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow each phase in sequence: identify candidate activities (inventory); examine special circumstances and exemptions (management review); develop PWS, MEO, and perform the cost study (cost comparison); then carry out the chosen option and address post-award transition and administration (implementation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory: identify non-excluded commercial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventory phase involves the identification of Navy activities ashore that can be performed by commercial sources. This includes all those functions that are not excluded because they are 'governmental in nature'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use functional coding (e.g., S713, T801) and a complete inventory listing to ensure all potentially commercial functions are considered for study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management review: identify exemptions and special circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The management review phase ... involves systematic examination and analysis by the activity to identify any special circumstances that would preclude performance of the function by a commercial source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically determine national defense exemptions per OPNAVINST 4860.6C (mobilization/contingency, military training requirements, maintaining sea/shore rotation base, depot and intermediate maintenance) and consider case-by-case exemptions (core logistics functions, patient care).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The task analysis involved in the development of the PWS must identify and quantify the output generated by the function. 'Insofar as possible, the Statement of Work (PWS) is meant to specify work only in terms of its outcome, rather than in terms of the procedures used to achieve that outcome.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PWS must accurately reflect desired quality and performance, quantify outputs, and serve as the basis for both government and contractor cost estimates; use standard or generic PWSs where available to improve consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Requirements Summary (PRS) and Acceptable Quality Level (AQL)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS also includes a section known as the Performance Requirements Summary (PRS) which stipulates the performance standards or quality levels that must be met. Included in the PRS, in addition to the Acceptable Quality Level (AQL), is a deduction percentage which approximates the level of importance that the activity assigns to each of the performance measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRS items should be objectively measurable; assign deduction percentages to represent relative importance and allow for monetary assessments against contractor billings for non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective measurability and contractor quality control responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: These performance quality standards 'are designed to be objectively measurable, and quality control is part of the contractor's responsibility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write performance standards so they can be observed/measured; require contractors to implement Quality Control programs tied to PRS metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance for contractor and government performance documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Quality Assurance program is implemented using government employees known as Quality Assurance Evaluators (QAEs)... While a formal quality assurance program is not required for government performance, the MEO must provide a capability for evaluating and for clearly documenting government performance to the standards set by the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contracted out, implement government QA via QAEs/Contract Compliance Representatives conducting regular surveillance. If retained in-house, ensure the MEO can objectively document performance to PWS/PRS standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management study and creation of the Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The management study/review ... ensures that the in-house work force is organized and staffed as efficiently and effectively as possible... Once this review has been conducted, the organization is restructured into what is termed as the Most Efficient Organization or MEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct a management study to optimize structure, staffing, and procedures; MEO should reflect an 'all civilian' operation when used for cost comparison (convert military positions to civilian equivalents).

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house cost estimate requirements per Cost Comparison Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed guidance for preparation of this estimate is contained in the Cost Comparison Handbook. Category and line-by-line computational techniques are included in the handbook and include guidance on such factors as inflation, personnel costs, materials and supplies, depreciation, overhead, contract administration, conversion costs, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build the MEO cost estimate using the handbook's prescribed line items and computational techniques; ensure consistent treatment of inflation, personnel benefits, overhead, depreciation, conversion, and other cost categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of military positions in cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: If a function has been identified as a commercial activity, it represents a decision that the function does not require any Military positions... any military positions in the function under study '...shall be converted to civilian positions for cost comparison purposes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When costing the MEO, replace military billets with civilian equivalents and cost accordingly so the MEO reflects an all-civilian operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealed-bid comparison to lowest competent and responsive bidder
rubrics_metrics.description: Based upon the requirements of the PWS, the MEO is costed out ... and the estimate is presented to the Contracting Officer in a sealed bid. The government's bid ... is compared to that of the lowest, competent and responsive private bidder and a decision is made to either retain the function in-house ... or to contract out the function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sealed bids and compare MEO total cost to the lowest technically competent/responsive contractor bid (including contractor-side contract administration costs) to make the retain vs contract decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contract administration costs and MEO personnel add-ons
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor bids included an estimate of the contract administration costs (normally ranging from 4-8% of the MEO bid), but excluded the 10% of MEO personnel costs that are added before making the actual contract out decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contractor bids account for contract administration costs; apply any prescribed percentage additions to MEO personnel costs (e.g., 10%) per prevailing policy when comparing bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized cost factors and methodology (incremental vs full cost)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cost Comparison Handbook set forth standard cost factors and was intended to provide a uniform methodology ... cost comparison methodology was changed from the complex full cost method to a simpler incremental approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the standard cost factors and the methodology (incremental or other prescribed approach) established in the current Cost Comparison Handbook; be aware that methodology changes (full vs incremental) materially affect outcomes and dispute likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of retirement cost factor (controversial variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The retirement cost factor has continued to fluctuate and remains an area of controversy in the cost comparison process. ... Transmittal Memoranda changed the retirement factor several times (e.g., 7%, 24.7%, 14.1%, present level 27.05%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the current, officially prescribed retirement cost factor consistently; document and justify the factor used because it is a frequent source of contention in cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAO-identified credibility and process weaknesses to address
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO observed: (1) Complete and accurate in-house cost data is not readily available. (2) OMB Circular A-76 does not generally require cost comparisons to support contracting out decisions. (3) OMB Circular A-76 does not require cost comparisons on activities already contracted out to assure their continued cost effectiveness. (4) Uncertainty exists concerning the stability and accuracy of the Government retirement cost factor. (5) Uncertainty exists on whether in-house costs should be determined on an incremental or fully allocated basis. (6) Cost comparisons lack credibility in some cases because they are often prepared by personnel who are unqualified or would be affected by actions. (7) Required reviews of the commercial or industrial activities are far behind schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address these weaknesses proactively: ensure complete in-house cost data, require/track cost comparisons where appropriate, document choice of costing basis, use qualified and impartial personnel to prepare comparisons, and keep reviews on schedule to improve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of post-award/transaction costs and transition risks
rubrics_metrics.description: The CA program is defined in pre-award terms and provides little formal guidance for transition to the MEO or to the contractor. ... post-award transaction costs in excess of those anticipated by the pre-award cost comparison process are often ignored. ... no formal accounting system that captures litigation costs, conversion costs, contract administration costs in excess of that allowed for in the cost comparison process, quality or substandard performance costs, or the cost of contingency operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating contracting out, estimate and plan for post-award transaction costs (litigation, conversions, premium contract admin, quality failures, contingency/mobilization costs) and include contingency/transition plans (e.g., for contractor default, bankruptcy, or funding cuts) in decision-making and budgeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for Service Contract Act wage determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service Contract Act of 1965 provides for the establishment of minimum wages, benefits and working conditions for service contract employees... The wage determination serves as a bottom limit for the contractor on employee wages and in certain cases reduces some of the contractor's cost flexibility in contract competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cost comparisons and bid evaluations, apply relevant Department of Labor wage determinations for the geographic area and service class; recognize wage determinations can materially affect contractor pricing and subsequent comparisons.
